permits.summary: Attorney General Raúl Torrez told FERC its environmental assessment of the Green Chile pipeline is inadequate because it omits emissions from Project Jupiter, which he says cannot run without the pipeline, and argued NEPA calls for a fuller review.
permits.schedule_impact: Could complicate FERC's review of the pipeline, which Energy Transfer filings already show slipping to 2027.
permits.source: Source NM (via News From The States)

permits.agency: Village of Mount Pleasant Plan Commission / Village Board
permits.action: Plan Commission approves amended seven-building Microsoft site plan
permits.summary: The Plan Commission unanimously approved Microsoft's amended site plan, which reduces the January plan's nine data centers to seven while raising total floor area to over 5.8 million sq ft, with more than a dozen conditions, including one asking Microsoft to consider noise protection for part of the site.
permits.schedule_impact: A final Village Board vote is expected later in October; Microsoft says it will update the community before vertical construction and that the changes are meant to speed development.

permits.action: SELC petitions challenge Amazon and Duke generator air permits
permits.summary: For a local coalition, SELC filed petitions against the two minor-source permits that cover 649 diesel generators at Amazon's Hamlet campus (592 backup units for Amazon and 57 bridge-power units for Duke), arguing the state should have treated them as one major source.
permits.schedule_impact: If the petitions succeed, the generators could need major-source permitting; no hearing date is listed.

permits.action: Adopts six-month pause on data center development applications
permits.summary: Millington approved a six-month pause on development applications for industrial-scale computing, accessory computing and non-grid power generation; it took effect immediately and expires April 12 unless extended.
permits.schedule_impact: Applies only within Millington, which has not received a data center proposal.

permits.action: Moratorium for unincorporated county passes first reading 5-4
permits.summary: A temporary data center moratorium for unincorporated Shelby County, sponsored by Commissioners Erika Sugarmon and Henri Brooks, passed first reading 5-4 on Oct 12 and still needs further readings; length and terms were not reported.
permits.schedule_impact: Would apply only in unincorporated areas, where no projects are currently identified; no date for the next reading was reported.

permits.action: Data center zoning ordinance passes first of three readings
permits.summary: The Memphis City Council passed, on its consent agenda, a tentative data center zoning ordinance that combines several members' proposals; it needs two more full-council votes, and its terms were not described.
permits.schedule_impact: Memphis data center zoning rules remain unsettled until two more full-council votes.

permits.action: Data center code amendment (noise, cooling) postponed to Oct 19
permits.summary: Cheyenne's proposed data center code amendment (PLTA-26-5) would lower property-line noise limits, require sound studies, bar unenclosed rooftop fans, cap generator testing at 30 minutes per generator weekly and require closed-loop rather than evaporative cooling; on Oct 5 the Planning Commission postponed it to Oct 19 seeking more information on sound studies, setbacks and facility size.
permits.schedule_impact: Rules for data centers under Cheyenne's development code stay unsettled until at least Oct 19.

permits.action: Power-generation zoning amendment postponed again, to Nov 2
permits.summary: Cheyenne's proposed power-generation amendment (PLTA-26-3) would exempt small community generation up to 2.5 MW from some review and let emergency backup generators run up to 144 hours; on Oct 5 the Planning Commission voted 3-1 to postpone it to Nov 2, after an earlier postponement on Sept 8.
permits.schedule_impact: Leaves the city's rules for onsite power generation unsettled until at least November.

permits.action: Final approval of Orchard Hills data center annexation and rezoning
permits.summary: On third reading, Cheyenne's council approved annexation, agricultural zoning, rezoning to light industrial and a future land-use map change for a two-building Trammell Crow data center next to the Orchard Valley area, after a motion to delay failed 8-1 amid resident opposition.
permits.schedule_impact: Local zoning is settled; the failed delay was aimed at applying pending city data center rules, which may not reach this site.

permits.action: Final site plan approved 5-1 for Google campus
permits.summary: After nearly an hour of public comment, the planning commission voted 5-1 to approve the final site plan for the six-building, 1 GW campus on an industrially zoned 282-acre parcel, which Bridge describes as the last major permit hurdle.
permits.schedule_impact: Clears the main local approval; a recall effort against the township board is under way.

permits.action: DTE-Google 20-year supply and clean-capacity contracts approved
permits.summary: The commission approved DTE's special contracts for the Van Buren Township data center, with a 20-year term, 80% minimum billing demand, at least 15 years of minimum charges on early exit, collateral requirements, and Google funding up to 1,600 MW of renewables and 480 MW of batteries.
permits.schedule_impact: Supports electric service starting around December 2027 with full load by December 2028.

permits.action: Development and benefits agreement with Meta approved unanimously
permits.summary: The fiscal court unanimously approved a resolution on a 40-year, multi-phase agreement with Meta that includes county payments, water and sewer funding, a new Maysville treatment plant and a public-safety payment, with phase-one construction expected within three years.
permits.schedule_impact: Removes the main local deal hurdle; actual start timing remains open-ended.

permits.action: More than 2,000 acres rezoned for data-center campus
permits.summary: WCPO reports the fiscal court approved zoning of more than 2,000 acres for the campus in May 2026 and that a residents' lawsuit to block construction has since been filed.
permits.schedule_impact: Zoning is in place, but the pending lawsuit could delay work if a court intervenes.

permits.action: Annexation and development agreement approved 5-0
permits.summary: The council voted 5-0 to annex the 664-acre Taylor Technology Campus under a 20-year development agreement, giving local approval to a gas-powered campus of up to 1 GW.
permits.schedule_impact: Local approval is in place, but a state permit freeze and resident opposition could affect the 2028 first-power target.

permits.action: TCEQ letter confirms data-center permit issuance remains paused
permits.summary: In an October 19 letter, TCEQ's interim executive director said the agency had paused issuing permits for infrastructure directly supporting data centers and was screening applications, although agency records show it kept reviewing some power-plant applications, granted some stormwater coverage and mailed some public notices after September 21.
permits.schedule_impact: New TCEQ permits for data-center campuses and their power plants appear frozen with no end date set, though some earlier-stage processing has continued.

permits.agency: Office of the Texas Attorney General
permits.action: AG sends water-use reporting letters to 156 data-center developments
permits.summary: The Attorney General's office notified 156 data-center developments in 32 counties, including El Paso, Williamson and Pecos, that they must supply current and accurate water-use data, as part of a wider probe that covers sites that did not answer the Texas Water Development Board's water-use survey.
permits.schedule_impact: Developments that do not report water use could face state enforcement; the release names no companies and sets no deadline.
permits.source: Office of the Texas Attorney General

permits.action: TCEQ mails preliminary-decision notice for VoltaGrid ABI-1 plant
permits.summary: TCEQ mailed a preliminary-decision notice for VoltaGrid's ABI-1 gas plant serving Vantage's Shackelford County campus on September 22, the day after the governor's pause order, and publication on September 23 opened a 30-day public comment period.
permits.schedule_impact: The plant permit has moved toward a decision, but no final permit is reported and the statewide pause may hold back issuance.

permits.action: Denies developer's writ to force Lordstown site-plan review
permits.summary: In State ex rel. Bristolville 25 Developer v. Lordstown (2026-Ohio-4073, case 2025-1497), all seven justices joined a per curiam opinion. It held that the village's data-center moratorium suspended any duty to review the developer's site plan, and that the developer had no vested right to the earlier zoning because it had never applied for a permit.
permits.schedule_impact: Upholds Lordstown's moratorium, so the separate Bristolville four-building data center proposal stays on hold under village rules for now.

permits.action: Public meeting on proposed data center conditional-use zoning
permits.summary: Trustees set an Oct. 28 public meeting on zoning commission language that would allow data centers only as conditional uses, with setback, noise, water and screening rules. Large facilities of 10 MW or more of critical IT load would need conditional use permits. Trustees then have 20 days to adopt or reject it, and a resident has turned in 501 signatures opposing data centers.
permits.schedule_impact: Would add conditional-use review for data centers in a Trumbull County township near Lordstown; no direct effect on the Lordstown site is reported.

permits.action: Begins drafting data center zoning regulations
permits.summary: Champion Township's zoning board in Trumbull County started drafting data center rules because its code has none. No developer has approached the township, but members named the former Copperweld Steel property as the likeliest site.
permits.schedule_impact: Early-stage local rule-making in the Lordstown area; no effect on the Lordstown site is reported.

permits.agency: Kentucky state economic development board / Mason County
permits.action: 40-year bond tax exemption; state sales-tax break awaits board approval
permits.summary: The county plans 40-year industrial revenue bonds that would remove the campus from local property taxes in exchange for annual payments of about $5 million to the county and $2 million to schools. A state economic development board is to rule on a sales tax break on equipment later in October, which a think tank puts at more than $400 million for the first phase.
permits.schedule_impact: Incentives affect project economics more than schedule; some lawmakers have floated rolling back the sales tax break next session.

permits.action: Unanimously approves Invenergy's Red Oak Ridge gas plant
permits.summary: Commissioners unanimously approved Invenergy's applications for the nearly 1.2 GW Red Oak Ridge Energy Center in Kenosha County and the 324 MW Foundry Ridge plant in Walworth County, gas plants tied to rising data center demand that We Energies has applied to acquire.
permits.schedule_impact: Red Oak Ridge is targeted to come online in 2030, so it adds regional supply only late in the decade.

permits.action: Hearing on NPDES permit for onsite sanitary wastewater plant
permits.summary: EGLE held a public hearing on a draft discharge permit that would let the data center's onsite plant release treated employee sanitary wastewater to the Saline River, with a 0.2 mg/L phosphorus limit, no PFAS monitoring, and no cooling or other industrial water allowed; comments closed at midnight Oct 23.
permits.schedule_impact: Covers only staff sanitary waste; EGLE said other permits may still be needed for cooling water, water withdrawals or nearby waterways, and no decision date was given.

permits.action: DNR settles suit, agrees to full EISs for data centers
permits.summary: To settle the Sierra Club and Midwest Environmental Advocates suit over its permits for Vantage's Port Washington campus, DNR agreed to do full environmental impact statements for individual data center proposals from now on and a statewide analysis of data center resource use.
permits.schedule_impact: The settlement applies to future proposals and is not reported to alter the Port Washington build, but new Wisconsin data center projects may face longer state environmental reviews.

permits.action: One-year data center moratorium fails on 6-6 vote
permits.summary: At its Oct 20, 2026 meeting the Memphis City Council split 6-6 on Ordinance 19, the proposed 12-month data center moratorium, so it did not pass; one member was absent.
permits.schedule_impact: No year-long citywide freeze on new data centers will take effect under this ordinance.

permits.action: Approves 135-day pause on data center permitting
permits.summary: After rejecting the longer moratorium, the council on Oct 20, 2026 approved legislation from Councilman Jeff Warren and Councilwoman Rhonda Logan that includes a 135-day pause in data center permitting while officials review effects on neighborhoods and infrastructure.
permits.schedule_impact: New Memphis data center permits may be held up for about four and a half months; the source does not give start or end dates or say whether existing projects are covered.

permits.action: Data center regulations ordinance passes third and final reading
permits.summary: On Oct 20, 2026 the council passed on final reading an ordinance sponsored by Councilman Warren regulating large data centers, including limits on routine evaporative and once-through cooling, closed-loop water requirements, a carbon-based electricity phase-out schedule and rules for expanding existing sites.
permits.schedule_impact: Could constrain cooling design and expansion of Memphis data centers; how the rules apply to existing xAI facilities is not stated in the source.

permits.action: Judge rejects DOJ bid to dismiss NAACP turbine suit
permits.summary: Judge Debra Brown let the federal government intervene in the NAACP's Clean Air Act case over xAI's 69 Southaven turbines but refused its request to dismiss, saying EPA's enforcement role does not give it full control of the litigation.
permits.schedule_impact: The suit, which asks the court to stop unpermitted turbine operation, continues; no next hearing date was reported.

permits.action: Recommends six code sections, including data center water-use estimates
permits.summary: Cheyenne's Planning Commission sent six development-code sections to the City Council, among them a rule that data center site plans estimate monthly water use in gallons, a 1,000-foot setback for workforce housing, defined day and night hours, and construction noise and lighting rules, while holding back the separate data center section.
permits.schedule_impact: The six sections go to the City Council for introduction on Oct. 26; they would add water-use disclosure and construction-period limits for data center projects in the city if adopted.

permits.action: Commission returns OG&E large-load tariff to ALJ; hearing January 2027
permits.summary: In a 3-0 vote, commissioners dropped the plan for a November decision, adopted Commissioner Hiett's proposed order sending OG&E's HB 2992 large-load tariff case back to an administrative law judge, and set a hearing on the merits for 9 a.m. on January 12, 2027. The order says the responsive testimony raised substantial legal and jurisdictional questions.
permits.schedule_impact: The tariff that will govern new 75 MW-plus OG&E loads is unlikely to be settled before early 2027.

permits.action: SB 259 bars non-recirculating evaporative groundwater cooling at data centers
permits.summary: The Groundwater Modernization Act, signed May 20 and taking effect November 1, stops data centers from using groundwater in open-air evaporative or other non-recirculating cooling. To get a groundwater permit, a data center must show low-consumption cooling such as closed-loop or dielectric immersion. Permit holders must file annual water-use reports with the Oklahoma Water Resources Board, which is to write rules on waste complaints and overuse penalties.
permits.schedule_impact: From November 1 it adds cooling-design and reporting conditions for any Oklahoma data center that seeks its own groundwater permit.

permits.action: Microgrid air permit hearing set to open Dec. 7
permits.summary: Scheduling orders filed Oct. 16 set the public hearing on the campus microgrid's air permit to begin Dec. 7 at the Sunland Park Multi-Generational Center, after an Oct. 26 hearing on a motion to dismiss tied to new pollutant figures and an Oct. 29 hearing on discovery.
permits.schedule_impact: The microgrid's air permit will not be decided before the December hearing, and dismissal of the application remains possible.
